messages.content: We’re looking at Charleston for spring break. Compare leaving Chicago late Thursday, March 26, and coming back Monday evening against leaving Friday morning, March 27, and coming back Tuesday. Three of us. I want the whole cost difference and how much time we actually get there. Don’t book anything.

I’ll compare March 26-30 with March 27-31 for three travelers, including round-trip airfare, hotel nights, and realistic arrival and airport-departure times. Before I price it, are you thinking downtown Charleston, or should I use a broader lodging area for the first pass?
Use downtown for now. We can get into neighborhoods after we settle the dates.

For the Thursday-Monday pattern, the strongest nonstop schedule I found leaves O’Hare at 7:05 p.m. Thursday and lands in Charleston at 10:18 p.m. The return leaves Charleston at 6:10 p.m. Monday and reaches O’Hare at 7:44 p.m. Economy is $428 per person, or $1,284 for all three. A downtown room for Thursday through Monday is broadly $1,180-$1,720 including estimated taxes for four nights. That puts flights and lodging at $2,464-$3,004 before local transportation and meals.
And the Friday option?

The best comparable nonstop leaves O’Hare at 8:20 a.m. Friday and arrives at 11:31 a.m. The Tuesday return departs Charleston at 4:55 p.m. and arrives at O’Hare at 6:31 p.m. Airfare is $356 per person, totaling $1,068 for three. Downtown lodging from Friday through Tuesday is also four nights, currently about $1,090-$1,610 with estimated taxes. Flights plus hotel come to roughly $2,158-$2,678.
Wait, I was counting Thursday to Monday as five hotel nights because we’re leaving on five different calendar days.

It is four hotel nights: Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, with checkout Monday. Friday through Tuesday is likewise four nights: Friday through Monday, with checkout Tuesday. The Thursday itinerary spans parts of five calendar dates, but it does not create a fifth hotel night.
Got it. Then why is Friday cheaper on the hotel too? I expected Monday night to be worse than Thursday night.

Monday night is somewhat higher than Thursday at several properties, but the Friday-Tuesday stay avoids the more expensive Thursday-night inventory showing at a few downtown hotels and has slightly better four-night package pricing. The difference is not uniform: at some hotels Friday-Tuesday is only $20-$40 less, while at others it is about $120 less. That is why I’d keep the lodging comparison as a range until we choose a neighborhood and specific room.
How much usable Charleston time do we get in each case? Don’t count sleeping or sitting at the airport as vacation time.

Using hotel arrival and airport-departure cutoffs, Thursday-Monday gives almost no useful Thursday time. Landing at 10:18 p.m. should mean reaching a downtown hotel around 11:10-11:35 p.m. On Monday, leaving downtown around 3:45 p.m. is prudent for the 6:10 flight. That produces three full days, Friday through Sunday, plus about 8:00 a.m.-3:45 p.m. Monday: approximately 39 hours 45 minutes of usable daytime in the city.
And Friday through Tuesday?

With the 11:31 a.m. Friday arrival, you should reach downtown around 12:35-1:00 p.m. Tuesday’s 4:55 p.m. flight calls for leaving downtown around 2:30 p.m. Counting Friday from 1:00-8:00 p.m., three full days Saturday through Monday, and Tuesday from 8:00 a.m.-2:30 p.m., the practical total is about 37 hours 30 minutes. So Thursday-Monday yields roughly 2 hours 15 minutes more usable daytime, despite the late Thursday arrival.
That’s closer than I expected. Put the totals next to each other and include airport transportation in Charleston. We won’t rent a car.

For a downtown stay, I’d allow $90-$130 total for two airport rides, depending on surge pricing and pickup location. Thursday-Monday: flights $1,284, hotel $1,180-$1,720, airport rides $90-$130, total $2,554-$3,134. Friday-Tuesday: flights $1,068, hotel $1,090-$1,610, rides $90-$130, total $2,248-$2,808. The Friday-Tuesday pattern is therefore about $306 cheaper at the low end and $326 cheaper at the high end.
Add Chicago parking too. We’d drive to O’Hare, and use a reasonable economy-lot estimate.

Allowing about $90 for four days of O’Hare economy parking, Thursday-Monday becomes $2,644-$3,224. Friday-Tuesday also spans four parking nights at roughly $90, becoming $2,338-$2,898. The estimated gap remains $306-$326 because the parking duration is effectively the same.
What happens if the Thursday flight is delayed? That late arrival feels like it could wipe out the only advantage.

A one-hour delay would not reduce the counted daytime because Thursday night was already excluded. The real risk is a cancellation or major delay that pushes arrival into Friday. If you did not reach downtown until late Friday morning, the Thursday-Monday option would fall to roughly 32 usable hours and still cost more. The Friday morning itinerary has its own disruption risk, but there are more same-day recovery possibilities than with the last useful Thursday departure.
Is there an earlier Thursday nonstop that doesn’t require taking the whole day off? Say after 4:30.

There is a 5:15 p.m. nonstop arriving at 8:29 p.m., but it is $497 per person, or $1,491 for three. You would likely reach downtown around 9:25 p.m. It adds perhaps 90 minutes of usable evening at most and raises airfare by $207 total over the 7:05 p.m. flight. Including hotel, rides, and parking, that version would run about $2,851-$3,431.

No, that doesn’t earn the extra money. Just so I understand the five-night number before we move on: what would Thursday through Tuesday cost if we combined the earlier departure date with the later return?

Using the 7:05 p.m. Thursday outbound and 4:55 p.m. Tuesday return, airfare is about $1,350 total for three. Five downtown hotel nights are broadly $1,390-$2,020 including estimated taxes. Add $90-$130 for Charleston airport rides and about $110 for five nights of O’Hare parking, and the combined estimate is $2,940-$3,610. It would provide about 48 usable daytime hours, but it costs roughly $602-$712 more than Friday-Tuesday.

Then Friday to Tuesday is the right structure. The roughly two hours we lose isn’t worth more than $300, and the late Thursday flight has more downside. Keep the four-night and five-night hotel ranges available when we compare neighborhoods, but use Friday March 27 through Tuesday March 31 as the dates. Still don’t buy anything.

Friday, March 27 through Tuesday, March 31 is selected for the Charleston search, with no purchase made. The working nonstop flights are ORD-CHS 8:20-11:31 a.m. Friday and CHS-ORD 4:55-6:31 p.m. Tuesday, totaling $1,068 for three. Estimated arrival downtown is 12:35-1:00 p.m.; plan to leave downtown around 2:30 p.m. Tuesday. The four-night downtown lodging range is $1,090-$1,610, and the broader five-night reference is $1,390-$2,020. With $90-$130 for Charleston airport rides and about $90 for O’Hare parking, the selected trip currently totals $2,338-$2,898. The next step is a neighborhood-level hotel comparison.
